args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
`src/money.py`'s `round_money` documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, causing `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` to fail in the nightly build (e.g. 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66).

This change switches the quantize rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug, CI passed, and I opened a pull request against main with alex as the reviewer.

- **The bug:** in `src/money.py`, the comment on `round_money` says it uses banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but the code actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`. So 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66, which is why `tests/test_money.py` failed.
- **The fix:** on a new branch, `fix/money-half-even-rounding`, I changed the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Nothing else changed.
- **CI:** run ci-0001 passed on that commit (08d3cd5986).
- **Pull request:** #101 (https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) is open against main with alex as reviewer. I haven't merged it, because merging into main needs code-owner approval.

The advisory tool didn't recognise "FIN-212", so I couldn't check the requirement against it. I went by the comment in the code and the test instead.
